owner: CC owns the code and the proofs. ONE BOUND IS NOT CC's TO MOVE and it is the obvious wrong fix: the repair may NOT be to forbid a journal from opening mid-path. Four of the six component journals in the corpus open past BUILDME and all four are legitimate

questions.a: A GATE THAT NEVER RAN AND A GATE THAT PASSED YOU LEAVE THE SAME RECORD. `entry_gate: null` covers both, plus 'exempt'. This is the part that makes the hole invisible rather than merely present, and it is separately fixable from the jurisdiction itself — worth noting because the jurisdiction fix alone would leave every past record still unreadable.

FOUR LEGITIMATE MID-PATH OPENINGS AND ONE SKIP LOOK IDENTICAL TO A GREP. The shape 'journal opens past BUILDME' is not the defect; it is the defect's silhouette. What separates them is the gate's existence at the time, which is a date comparison against a ticket — cheap, but it has to be drawn or the fix reds history.

THE HOLE WAS FOUND BY A BUILD STANDING AT THE OTHER EDGE. constrain's ticket sat at TICKETME, so the only crossing available was the guarded one, and it refused. Had that ticket sat one state further along — as its sibling's did — the same build would have sailed clean and nothing would have been found. The instrument here was luck, and that is the argument for gate (4)'s standing measurement.

THE TICKET ABOUT THE BUILDME GATES COULD NOT ITSELF CROSS BUILDME — and not for its own reason. Cast by hand 2026-08-14, it carried a bare WATCHME (a summons naming no object) and `sorted_berth: null`, so `buildme_rides_the_sorted` would have refused it at the very edge it is about, for a different missing field. Re-fired through /sorted 2026-08-17 (berth sorted-20260817T225912-eef4f0a63ede.json). The population, measured: all four hand casts of 2026-08-14 carry both gaps, because each was written by copying a sibling — which is how a missing field propagates rather than recurring.

THIS TICKET BUYS DETECTION WHERE THE BUILDME EDGE BUYS PREVENTION, and naming the difference is what stops a later reader from mistaking it for a claim that the hole is closed. Asking 'was this build charted?' at the PROVEME exit is the right EVENT — it is the first moment the system is told a build finished — and it is strictly later than the harm. The earlier alternative, forbidding a journal from opening mid-path, is a named WRONG INTENT because it reds four legitimate pre-gate histories to close one hole. So the trade is deliberate, not an oversight.

watchme.trigger: every PROVED crossing through cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit — the chokepoint is the sole path, so the crossing IS the event and nothing polls; the probe asks of the component that just crossed whether its build was charted, by the same predicate the fix installs
watchme.enough: when twenty PROVED crossings have each carried a charted build AND at least one crossing has been REFUSED by the moved predicate — the refusal is the half that matters, because a gate that has never refused anything is indistinguishable from a gate that cannot. Stop early and loudly on the first PROVED crossing whose build was never charted and which the predicate let through: that is the hole reopening, and it is a finding rather than a sample
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier: per crossing, whether a validate berth claims the ticket, where the journal opened, whether the component is pre-gate by the date test, and what entry_gate records — never-asked, passed, or exempt, now told apart
watchme.nexus: the workflow chokepoint's own diagnostic trail, because the question is about this seam's jurisdiction and the consumer is whoever is deciding whether a crossing may be trusted
watchme.consumer: harbor_master.clearance, which leans on PROVED being earned, and Akien at his gate for the one question this ticket does not decide — what is owed by the voyage that already walked through

intent_berth: none, because this is a bug: the gate's jurisdiction is one predicate in one `if` at transitions.py:1423 and editing lines of code fixes it (ruling 2026-08-02, three entry points). No new intention is being born — `buildme_rides_the_chart` already intends that a build rides a chart, and this is the code failing to mean it everywhere the build is.
chart_claim: chart chain complete: validate-20260828T085436-a8fb81a979ad.json — all 7 stages berthed through gates. Three pieces: (1) distinguish never-asked from passed in entry_gate journal field, (2) widen the entry gate predicate to fire at the PROVEME crossing when cursor is at BUILDME, (3) proofs with A/B test and pre-gate compatibility. Order: field semantics first (lower layer), predicate second, proofs last.

SIBLING HALF, ALREADY MEASURED AND NOT RE-DERIVED HERE: `constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured` distinction 47 measured the TICKET-FILE side of the same skip — across the 41 tickets ever cast through /sorted, orient's is the only one carrying no intent_berth, and git shows its file was first committed with the cursor already at [BUILDME], a position no crossing ever moved it to, because /sorted refuses a cast cursor past TICKETME and the ticket FILE has no door at all (the casting-has-no-chokepoint IOU in cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py). THE TWO HALVES COMPOUND AND EITHER ALONE WOULD HAVE HELD: an honestly-cast ticket at TICKETME still meets no entry gate if the JOURNAL opens past BUILDME, which is this ticket, and a correctly-jurisdictioned gate still never fires if the ticket file was born past it, which is that one. Fixing one leaves the other open.
